hook: Two transformer layers are necessary and sufficient to run depth-first search on graphs efficiently
summary: The paper proves that a one-layer transformer needs size growing as N squared on dense graphs to pick the next DFS child, while two layers do full DFS with N log N size. Deeper models gain an exponentially longer look-ahead horizon, and a two-layer model provably learns DFS by gradient flow. All results concern idealized transformers and curated training data, not production language models.
title: Transformers Provably Learn Graph Search: Training Dynamics and the Exponential Power of Depth
